test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 12 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which statement is correct for the elements of second period?

options.text: They do not have the same number of valence electrons, but they contain the same number of shells.
They have the same number of valence electrons, but they do not contain the same number of shells.
They do not have the same number of valence electrons and they do not contain the same number of shells.
They have the same number of valence electrons and they also contain the same number of shells.

solution:
The correct answer is __**They do not have the same number of valence electrons, but they contain the same number of shells.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **elements of the second period **are Lithium (Li), Beryllium (Be), Boron (B), Carbon (C), Nitrogen (N), Oxygen (O), Fluorine (F), and Neon (Ne).
 
• All these elements have the **same number of shells**, which is two.
 
• The **number of valence electrons in the elements of the second period increases **from 1 (Lithium) to 8 (Neon), except for Beryllium, which has only 2 valence electrons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Periods are the horizontal rows in the periodic table that represent the number of electron shells in an element's atom.
 
• The number of electron shells in a row is the same for every element.
 
• Every subsequent element in a period is less metallic than the one before it and has one extra proton.
